label: Code and engineering
_comment: Automated checks outrank every score in this file. Pass them in as objective_checks; when they point at a side, the rubric is not consulted for the verdict.

criteria.label: Correctness
criteria.description: Does it do what the brief asked, including the edge cases the brief names? Reason about the actual control flow, not the naming.

criteria.label: Tests and verifiability
criteria.description: Are the changes covered by tests that would actually fail if the behaviour regressed? A test that cannot fail scores zero here.

criteria.label: Security
criteria.description: Injection, secret handling, authorisation, unvalidated input, unsafe deserialisation, path traversal.

criteria.label: Fit to the existing architecture
criteria.description: Does it use the project's existing helpers, layering and conventions rather than introducing a parallel way of doing the same thing?

criteria.label: Readability and maintenance
criteria.description: Would a colleague understand the intent in one read? Naming, structure, comment density matching the surrounding file.

criteria.label: Performance
criteria.description: Algorithmic cost, redundant IO, work inside hot loops. Only counts where the brief implies it matters.

criteria.label: Minimal change surface
criteria.description: Does it change only what the task requires? Penalise drive-by refactors and unrelated reformatting.

hard_failures.label: Breaks the stated tests
hard_failures.description: The candidate contradicts a test result supplied in the brief or in the objective checks.

hard_failures.label: Introduces a security hole
hard_failures.description: Leaks a secret, disables a guard, or opens an injection or traversal path.

hard_failures.label: Hard-coded secret
hard_failures.description: Embeds an API key, token, password or connection string in source.

hard_failures.label: Violates a stated hard requirement
hard_failures.description: Ignores an explicit constraint from the brief — a forbidden dependency, a required interface, a protected file.

hard_failures.label: Invented API
hard_failures.description: Calls a function, flag or field that does not exist in the supplied source material.
